scores.claim_text: GE Aerospace has U.S. government contracts subject to FAR/DFARS via its Defense & Propulsion Technologies segment.
scores.M_check: Mode A: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts(General Electric Company) + Mode B variant: GE Aviation Systems LLC
scores.M_value: General Electric Company: 13,752 DoD awards / $12.19B total. Top awards: AETP ($2.09B), F-15EX propulsion ($1.24B), Improved Turbine Engine EMD ($863M), F414-GE-400 LRIP ($834M), F414 EA-18G ($699M), T408 ($673M). GE Aviation Systems LLC: 4,023 awards / $684M. All named engine programs are confirmed.
scores.interpretation: Mode A passes cleanly: massive federal contracting footprint with named GE engine programs (F414, F404/F-15EX, T408, AETP/XA100, ITE/T901) directly tied to disclosure. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Total RPO of $190.6B; DPT RPO ~$20.7B at year-end 2025.
scores.M_check: Mode A: sec_filings confirms 2026-01-29 10-K on file; Mode B: usaspending obligations vs RPO gap check
scores.M_value: sec_filings.list_filings_by_form returned 10-K filed 2026-01-29 (accession 0000040545-26-000008). DoD obligated to GE Co alone ~$12.19B life-to-date — well below $20.7B DPT RPO (consistent with multi-year ramp + non-DoD defense/international portion). Mode B gap is reasonable given defense + non-US gov mix.
scores.interpretation: RPO disclosure passes Mode A; Mode B gap-check shows DoD obligated $$ is meaningfully less than DPT RPO but consistent (RPO includes future deliveries on long-cycle engine LRIP programs not yet obligated, plus foreign military sales). PASS.

scores.claim_text: GE Aerospace maintains a growing patent portfolio underpinning competitive advantage.
scores.M_check: Mode A: uspto_odp.query_assignee(General Electric Company); Mode B: GE Aerospace + GE Aviation variants
scores.M_value: General Electric Company: 24,759 applications / 12,617 granted. GE Aviation: 943 / 606 granted. GE Aerospace (new naming after rename): 9 / 2 granted (small because the rebrand is recent). Patents are concentrated on turbofan engines, gas turbine engines, gearbox, propulsor — directly relevant to claimed competitive areas.
scores.interpretation: Far exceeds the 5-granted threshold; engine-relevant claims dominate. Note: only 2 granted patents under literal 'GE Aerospace' assignee name (entity-resolution caveat) but legacy 'General Electric Company' and 'GE Aviation Systems' assignments cover the gap. PASS.

'General Electric' in OH returns 51 facilities including Evendale Altitude Test Facility. scores.claim_text: Delivered 2,386 commercial engines (1,802 LEAP) in 2025 with $1B MRO investment in progress.
scores.M_check: Mode A: implicit (no direct unit-count registry); Mode B: corroborating manufacturing-facility OSHA records + EPA presence + DoD contract continuity demonstrates active production
scores.M_value: OSHA Vandalia, OH GE Aviation Systems site shows 378 employees in NAICS 336320 (engine parts manufacturing); EPA Evendale flagship plant active; DoD obligation flow (most recent F414 LRIP 2023 N0001923C0013 $673M) consistent with active production. No direct unit-count registry exists for civil engine deliveries — claim is verifiable only via FAA TC data and OEM disclosure.
scores.interpretation: Mode B presence/operational verification supports the production claim. Volume specifics are not independently verifiable via M registries. PASS (operationally corroborated).

scores.claim_text: Two major separations in two years (GE HealthCare Jan 2023; GE Vernova Apr 2024) — material structural reorganization.
scores.M_check: Mode A: sec_filings shows 8-Ks dated 2023-01-04 and 2024-04-02 referencing both separation agreements; Mode B: claim_evolution(material weakness) and (airworthiness directive)
scores.M_value: sec_filings returned 50 GE filings 2023-2026 confirming separation 8-Ks. claim_evolution(material weakness) returned 3 mentions, all classified UNRELATED (boilerplate audit-opinion language only; no actual ICFR material weakness has been disclosed). adverse_findings=[], AFFIRMED=0. claim_evolution(airworthiness directive) = SILENT_POST_CLAIM (0 hits).
scores.interpretation: Separations verified; ICFR check clean — no material weakness language. Despite the corporate complexity, registry does not show audit-opinion deterioration. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Counterparty disclosure — GE Aerospace is a prime engine supplier to defense primes (LMT, NOC, BA).
scores.M_check: Mode B: edgar_fts.query_fulltext('GE Aerospace', cik=COUNTERPARTY_CIK) for LMT (0000936468), Boeing (0000012927), Northrop Grumman (0001133421)
scores.M_value: Lockheed Martin: 10 hits (10-K, 10-Q mentions including 2026-01-29 10-K). Boeing: 1 hit (DEF 14A 2026-03-06 only). Northrop Grumman: 0 hits.
scores.interpretation: LMT cross-mentions cleanly verified — strong Mode B confirmation. Boeing's single mention in only a proxy statement is light given GEnx is a Boeing 787/747-8 engine and CFM LEAP powers 737 MAX (via the CFM JV with Safran). Northrop Grumman's zero hits is notable since B-21 engine is widely understood as GE (rumored F118-derivative). However: (a) B-21 program details are classified — NOC may legitimately not disclose engine supplier in public filings, and (b) CFM LEAP appears in Boeing filings under the CFM JV name not 'GE Aerospace' — so this is name-variant fragility (heuristic 6), not a true absence. Per heuristic 7 the disclosure threshold is not met for SEVE. MODERATE.

scores.claim_text: FAA type certificates / production certificate / repair-station certificates held — regulatory status claim.

scores.M_value: EPA FRS confirms Evendale + other OH facilities. claim_evolution('airworthiness directive') returned SILENT_POST_CLAIM with 0 hits (no AD escalation language in 2024-2026 GE filings). The M-source catalog does not include a direct FAA TC / PC / RS registry source.
scores.interpretation: FAA certificate status is not in the catalog (out of M-source scope). Indirect proxy (claim_evolution for AD language) shows no escalation. Catalog coverage gap — UNVERIFIABLE per rubric. (No adverse signal either.)

scores.claim_text: Insider Form-4 behavior around defense-budget / corporate events.
scores.M_value: Signal: CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY. 49 Form-4 filings, 36 total sales, $109M total; 14 proximate sales worth $13.55M; 6 DISCRETIONARY (non-10b5-1) proximate sales by 4 unique insiders (Stokes, Gowder, Procacci, Giglietti) within 14 days of FY26 bipartisan budget signing (2026-01-20). Top single sale: Russell Stokes sold 21,469 shares at $306.46 = $6.58M on 2026-01-30 (just 10 days after the budget event), plus another 8,894 shares same day ($2.73M). Gowder sold $1.22M on 2026-02-02 (13 days post). Giglietti sold $608K on 2026-01-30. None coded as 10b5-1 — all discretionary.
scores.interpretation: Per the framework heuristic, CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY signal is the highest-signal flag and warrants SEVE-RED. Four insiders selling >$11.7M in discretionary stock within two weeks of the FY26 budget signing — coinciding with the 10-K filing window (2026-01-29) — is the canonical Mode B signal. The CEO of Defense & Systems (Gowder), the CEO of Propulsion & Additive Technologies (Procacci), the CEO of Commercial Engines & Services (Stokes), and the Chief Accounting Officer / Treasurer (Giglietti) all sold. Marking SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY (Mode B-only Tier-1 signal; not RED because GE has clean Mode A registry coverage and the sales may reflect post-vesting equity rebalancing rather than information asymmetry, but the cluster is unambiguous and per framework rubric is the highest-signal Mode B flag).
